stemBlocks.value: Given the column vectors WX = (5, −1), XY = (−3, 7) and ZY = (8, −7), determine each of the following: (i) a vector other than (5, −1) that is parallel to WX, (ii) WY, (iii) XZ, (iv) |XY|.
Think first: Column vectors add and subtract component by component, and the only trap here is that ZY points the wrong way for the route you need in part (iii).

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p282-q05 from workbook page 282.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply WX by any scalar other than 1 to produce a parallel vector.

contentBlocks.value: 2 × (5, −1) = (10, −2); any multiple such as (15, −3) or (−5, 1) also works

solutionSteps.instruction: Add WX and XY component by component to get WY.
Reverse ZY to get YZ, since the route X → Y → Z needs YZ.
Apply Pythagoras to the components of XY.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply WX by any convenient scalar for (i); add WX and XY for WY; for XZ go X → Y → Z, using YZ = −ZY; then apply Pythagoras to the components of XY.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) (10, −2) — any non-zero multiple of (5, −1) other than itself  (ii) WY = (2, 6)  (iii) XZ = (−11, 14)  (iv) |XY| = √58 ≈ 7.62 units

whyThisWorks.value: Two vectors are parallel exactly when one is a scalar multiple of the other, so scaling the components keeps the direction and only changes the length. Adding vectors nose-to-tail cancels the middle letter — WX + XY leaves WY — which is why the components simply add. Reversing a vector flips the sign of both components, so ZY becomes YZ, and the magnitude is just the hypotenuse of the right triangle whose legs are the two components.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving (5, −1) itself, or the zero vector, as the parallel vector.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving (5, −1) itself, or the zero vector, as the parallel vector.

commonErrors.misconception: Using ZY directly in the chain X → Y → Z instead of reversing it to YZ.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using ZY directly in the chain X → Y → Z instead of reversing it to YZ.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding an x-component to a y-component when the columns are written horizontally.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding an x-component to a y-component when the columns are written horizontally.
